title: Assess regulatory approval before a product launch
summary: Before launching a product or business model whose licensing or regulatory classification is uncertain. A qualified market-by-market classification and approval plan with explicit no-launch conditions.
outcomes: A qualified market-by-market classification and approval plan with explicit no-launch conditions.
guidance: Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.
when: Before launching a product or business model whose licensing or regulatory classification is uncertain.

parts.title: Describe intended use and the complete business model
parts.guidance: Document claims, users, customer types, technology, funds or data handled and target markets. Include physical, health, financial, employment and other high-consequence uses that may change classification.

references.title: GOV.UK data protection and your business

execution.rationale: Prepare or reconcile the specified private evidence and documents; external changes and decisions use their own approved steps.

parts.title: Obtain a qualified classification and authority map
parts.guidance: Sector and local counsel identify the competent regulators, product or service classifications and possible exemptions. Record evidence and unresolved questions; a general startup guide cannot approve a clinical, financial or other licensed activity.

references.title: GOV.UK data protection and your business

execution.rationale: The accountable person performs the decision, expert assessment or personal interaction described in this step. Supporting preparation does not authorize that act.

approval.scope: Obtain a qualified classification and authority map

parts.title: Prepare the approval and evidence workplan
parts.guidance: List the specific testing, quality, capital, personnel, documentation and application work identified by specialists. Assign accountable owners, dependencies and expert workstreams rather than estimating permission from a marketing category.

references.title: GOV.UK data protection and your business

parts.title: Authorize specialist submissions and pre-launch controls
parts.guidance: Qualified teams prepare and submit the required applications after proper review and authorization. Record authority decisions and operating restrictions and keep unapproved activities and claims blocked.

references.title: GOV.UK data protection and your business

parts.title: Review the exact permitted launch scope
parts.guidance: The accountable specialists confirm permissions, conditions and operating readiness for each market. Approve only the evidenced scope and establish monitoring and reassessment when the product, claims or business model change.

notes.text: This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.
